text:
Recent work supports timestamp conditioning, but the retrieved results do not establish a validated time-aware NextItNet variant. [TGCL4SR (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28789) embeds interaction intervals in its sequence encoder; [E-NSDE (NeurIPS 2024)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/7cdbd53dfbcf9a5263227555aac5b9cd-Abstract-Conference.html) models continuous preference evolution and interval-dependent uncertainty. [TimeWeaver (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-8954/13/10/857) combines convolutional temporal modeling with temporal calibration of positional encodings. These motivate distinguishing elapsed time from sequence distance; their reported gains do not establish benefits under this Amazon benchmark.

Practical hypothesis: preserve [NextItNet’s dilated residual convolution backbone](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163), and condition each block on bucketed log-transformed historical time gaps through learned channel gates or feature modulation. A more direct variant gates each causal convolution tap using the elapsed time between its source and destination interactions, allowing equal sequence distances to receive different temporal weights. These are proposed adaptations, not verified mechanisms from the cited papers. Train all embeddings, gates and convolutions jointly within one model per category. Use only timestamps available in each prediction prefix; exclude the unknown next-interaction timestamp, mask padding, and read the final nonpadding position. Compare against the unchanged backbone using the fixed macro validation HR@10. First confirm timestamps can reach both training and deployed prediction through the supplied interfaces; item-only sequences cannot reliably recover user-specific elapsed times.
